The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-4}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x\in [-4,1)$ and the line segment for $x\in (1,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,1).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =ab \\  & =5(1) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-5.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,5].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4)(4) \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =-5+10 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
